clauses.clause: For a three-player standard game, how are aliens selected?
clauses.result: Each player is dealt two flares and the matching alien sheets, secretly chooses one alien, initially places it facedown, and returns the other sheet to the box. Apply any printed Game Setup instructions.

clauses.clause: Which flares enter the cosmic deck?
clauses.result: Add both flares dealt to every player, including the rejected aliens’ flares; add random extras if needed to reach ten flares total.

clauses.clause: How many cards does each player receive?
clauses.result: Deal each player an eight-card hand.

clauses.clause: How is the first player selected?
clauses.result: Draw destiny until a player color appears; that player starts. Shuffle that card back into the destiny deck, and ordinary play then passes left.

clauses.clause: What counts as one colony?
clauses.result: One or more ships of one color on one planet form one colony; extra ships there do not add colonies.

clauses.clause: Can several players have colonies on one planet?
clauses.result: Yes. Several colors can coexist on the same planet, each with its own colony.

clauses.clause: Do five foreign colonies have to be in different systems?
clauses.result: No. Five foreign planets may all be in one other system.

clauses.clause: Must offense retrieve a warp ship if available?
clauses.result: Yes. Offense must retrieve one of its ships from the warp if available.

clauses.clause: Where does the original rulebook place it when offense has colonies?
clauses.result: On any existing home or foreign colony.

clauses.clause: Where does the original rulebook place it when offense has none?
clauses.result: The original rulebook puts the retrieved ship directly in the gate when offense has no colonies.

clauses.clause: What happens when destiny has only one card left?
clauses.result: Do not draw the last card; shuffle it with the destiny discards, then draw from the new deck.

clauses.clause: What choice does drawing your own color offer if your home system contains a foreign colony?
clauses.result: Redraw, or target one chosen foreign colony in your home system; that colony’s owner is defense and other colonies there are bystanders.

clauses.clause: What choice does drawing your own color offer if your home system contains a completely empty planet?
clauses.result: Instead, aim at a home planet with no ships of any color and move up to four of your ships from any other existing home or foreign colonies there to reclaim it automatically. This is a win and successful encounter, proceeds only through Launch, and can qualify for a second encounter.

clauses.clause: Without a special power, may offense attack Blue’s foreign colony in Red’s home system after drawing Blue?
clauses.result: No. A color destiny targets that player in their own home system; ordinary rules do not let you attack a player’s foreign colony in a third player’s system.

clauses.clause: Who defends Red’s empty home planet if foreign bystanders are present?
clauses.result: Red, the home-system owner, defends even with zero ships on the target. Other colors’ colonies are bystanders and do not join the defense or suffer the encounter result.

clauses.clause: From where and how many ships may offense launch?
clauses.result: Offense commits one to four ships drawn from any combination of its existing home and foreign colonies, placing them on the wide end of the hyperspace gate.

clauses.clause: May offense strip a colony?
clauses.result: Yes, but removing its last ship immediately eliminates that colony.

clauses.clause: Can defense move ships onto or off the targeted planet during Launch?
clauses.result: No. Defense cannot add or subtract ships on the target during Launch.

clauses.clause: In what order are allies invited and committed?
clauses.result: Offense names invited allies first and they wait to answer; defense then invites. Starting left of offense and going clockwise, each other player answers one invitation or declines all, then commits before the next player decides.

clauses.clause: Can someone invited by both sides join both?
clauses.result: No. Each player may join only one side or neither.

clauses.clause: Where do defensive allies put their ships?
clauses.result: They commit one to four ships from any of their colonies beside the target planet, not on it.

clauses.clause: Who wins when offense has attack 10 and six ships, while defense has attack 12 and four ships?
clauses.result: The totals tie at 16 each: offense 10 + 6 = 16; defense 12 + 4 = 16. Defense wins ties.

clauses.clause: What happens to offense, offensive allies, defense, defensive allies and bystanders?
clauses.result: Offense and offensive ally ships go to the warp. The defending and bystander colonies stay. Defensive allies return their committed ships to any of their existing own colonies; helping does not give them a colony on the defended planet.

clauses.clause: When offense wins an attack, where do ships on each side go?
clauses.result: Offense and offensive ally ships land on the target; defense and defensive ally ships go to the warp.

clauses.clause: Do existing bystander colonies survive?
clauses.result: Yes. Bystanders survive the encounter.

clauses.clause: Does reinforcing an existing colony earn another colony?
clauses.result: No. Advance a colony marker only for a newly established foreign colony, not reinforcement of an existing colony.

clauses.clause: May a defensive ally combine cards and warp retrieval as rewards for three contributed ships?
clauses.result: Yes. The ally receives one defender reward per contributed ship, choosing for each reward either one cosmic-deck card or retrieval of one own warp ship; it may mix the choices, and cannot decline the rewards.

clauses.clause: Where do the allied ships go?
clauses.result: The defensive ally’s committed ships return to any existing colonies of that ally, even colonies different from their origins.

clauses.clause: Where do retrieved ships go?
clauses.result: Each retrieved warp ship may be placed on any colony belonging to that ally.

clauses.clause: If a main player’s negotiate loses to attack and that player loses three ships to warp while two allied ships also go there, how much compensation is collected?
clauses.result: The losing main player collects compensation for its own three ships actually lost to the warp; allied losses are excluded.

clauses.clause: From where is compensation collected?
clauses.result: The losing main player randomly takes the cards from the opponent’s hand, without seeing their faces.

clauses.clause: What if the opponent holds fewer cards than the compensation amount?
clauses.result: Take the opponent’s entire hand.

clauses.clause: When both reveal negotiate, what happens to allies?
clauses.result: Both sides’ allies return their ships to their own colonies; they gain nothing and cannot participate in the deal.

clauses.clause: What may the main players exchange, and where may a new colony be granted?
clauses.result: For one minute, they may transfer cards from their hands and/or each grant the other one colony on a planet where the giver already has a colony, including a foreign colony. The recipient may use any own ships not in the warp.

clauses.clause: What makes a valid deal?
clauses.result: At least one card or colony must actually transfer; a deal may be one-sided, but the players cannot agree to do nothing. Tangible terms are limited to permitted cards/colonies and specific exceptions; future promises are unenforceable.

clauses.clause: What are the failure penalty and time limit?
clauses.result: The main players have one minute. If time expires without agreement, each loses three ships of their choice to the warp, and offense cannot take an ordinary second encounter.

clauses.clause: What does Morph copy and when?
clauses.result: Morph becomes an exact copy of the opponent’s initially revealed encounter card: it copies an attack’s initial value, while a negotiate remains negotiate.

clauses.clause: Does Morph track later changes to the opponent’s card?
clauses.result: No. Later modifications do not automatically carry over; Morph can be modified separately.

clauses.clause: What happens after the encounter?
clauses.result: Morph returns to its normal identity and is normally discarded with the other revealed encounter card, unless an effect changes its destination.

clauses.clause: Who may play reinforcements and when?
clauses.result: Either main player and any ally may play reinforcements during Reveal after encounter cards are revealed.

clauses.clause: On which side may a reinforcement be played?
clauses.result: It adds its printed amount to either side’s total, including the opposing side.

clauses.clause: When is the reinforcement response window finished?
clauses.result: Players may answer with further reinforcements until all pass; then totals resolve.

clauses.clause: What is the ordinary per-player flare limit?
clauses.result: A player may play at most one flare per encounter.

clauses.clause: What is the ordinary per-card flare limit?
clauses.result: An individual flare may be used only once per encounter, even if it changes hands.

clauses.clause: When does a played flare return to hand?
clauses.result: Immediately after its effect finishes, unless its effect says otherwise.

clauses.clause: When does an alien use its own Wild instead of Super?
clauses.result: If it is your own alien’s flare and your power is available, you must use Super, not choose Wild. If your power is lost or zapped, only Wild is available.

clauses.clause: When offense lacks encounter cards at start of turn, what is the hand replacement?
clauses.result: Before Regroup effects on the first encounter of its turn, offense reveals and discards its remaining hand, then draws eight new cards.

clauses.clause: When defense lacks encounter cards at Planning, what is the replacement?
clauses.result: Defense reveals and discards the remaining hand and draws eight cards, repeating until it has an encounter card.

clauses.clause: When offense loses its last encounter card later, what happens to the hand and ships?
clauses.result: When offense needs an encounter card later in its turn and has none, the turn ends instead of drawing a replacement. Offense returns its committed ships to its own colonies; allies return their committed ships to their own colonies. Normal no-colony relocation applies, so ships with no existing colony to receive them go to the warp.

clauses.clause: Is playing other cards before the start-of-turn replacement compulsory?
clauses.result: No. Offense may first play legally playable non-encounter cards but is not required to do so.

clauses.clause: After a successful first encounter may offense start a second with no encounter card, hoping to obtain one later?
clauses.result: No. A second encounter requires at least one encounter card already in offense’s hand; it cannot start one hoping to obtain a card before Planning.

clauses.clause: What ends an ordinary turn after first or second encounter?
clauses.result: After an unsuccessful first encounter the turn passes left. After a successful first encounter offense may optionally take a second if it has an encounter card; after the second encounter the turn passes left. Machine is an exception.

clauses.clause: Exactly when is an ordinary alien power lost and regained for home-colony count?
clauses.result: With fewer than three home colonies, immediately turn the alien sheet facedown and lose its power. Restore it faceup when the player again occupies at least three home planets.

clauses.clause: Can it be used one last time upon loss?
clauses.result: No. The power is lost immediately; there is no last use.

clauses.clause: Does a Cosmic Zap stop every printed part of the sheet?
clauses.result: No. A Zap cancels the bold-italic use and prevents further uses that encounter, but non-use clauses remain active. Examples include Warrior gaining experience, Zombie liberating ships in a deal, and placing a Citadel.

clauses.clause: When contradictory effects really occur simultaneously, what player order resolves them?
clauses.result: Resolve offense first, then defense, then other players clockwise starting left of offense. Effects associated with no player resolve last.

clauses.clause: Can a player generally interrupt a resolving effect with another non-Zap action?
clauses.result: No. Finish one effect before starting another, except for a Zap or an effect expressly allowing interruption; only a Zap or specific interrupt may intervene once a hand-targeting effect begins.

clauses.clause: May a power be preemptively Cosmic Zapped?
clauses.result: No. A power may be Zapped only when it is being used, not preemptively.

clauses.clause: When are ordinary five-foreign-colony victories checked, and can wins be shared?
clauses.result: Check at the very end of Resolution; multiple players meeting the condition together share victory.

clauses.clause: What happens when Tick-Tock removes its last token because two main players make a deal that gives both their fifth foreign colony?
clauses.result: If the deal gives both main players their fifth foreign colony and removes Tick-Tock’s last token, all three share the win.

clauses.clause: What is the eligible role, optionality and phase for Amoeba?
clauses.result: Main player only; optional; Planning.

clauses.clause: What ship presence is required to Ooze?
clauses.result: Amoeba must have at least one ship in the encounter.

clauses.clause: When relative to card selection/reveal does it happen?
clauses.result: After encounter cards have been selected but before they are revealed.

clauses.clause: From/to where and how many ships may move?
clauses.result: Amoeba may remove some or all encounter ships to its colonies, or add any number of ships (even above the normal four) from any of its colonies into the encounter.

clauses.clause: Can a shipless winner receive a colony?
clauses.result: No. If Amoeba wins with no ships left in the encounter, it cannot receive a colony.

clauses.clause: What is the eligible role, optionality and phase for Anti-Matter?
clauses.result: Main player only; mandatory; Reveal.

clauses.clause: Which card pairing triggers Negation, and which side wins?
clauses.result: After both main players reveal attack cards, Anti-Matter uses its power to make the lower total win.

clauses.clause: How are own, opposing main-player and both sides’ allied ships counted?
clauses.result: Subtract the Anti-Matter player’s ships and all offensive and defensive allies’ ships from their appropriate sides’ attack cards; figure the opposing main player’s total normally.

clauses.clause: Which ordinary tie rule remains?
clauses.result: Defense still wins ties.

clauses.clause: What is the eligible role, optionality and phase for Barbarian?
clauses.result: Offense only; mandatory; Resolution.

clauses.clause: Which result triggers Loot and Pillage, and when relative to compensation?
clauses.result: After Barbarian wins an encounter, it uses the power before compensation is collected.

clauses.clause: Who sees/chooses how many cards?
clauses.result: Barbarian takes and looks at the opponent’s hand, then may choose one card for each of its own ships in the encounter.

clauses.clause: What happens to the remaining hand?
clauses.result: Afterward, discard the remainder of the opponent’s hand.

clauses.clause: What is the eligible role, optionality and phase for Calculator?
clauses.result: Main player only; optional; Planning.

clauses.clause: When is equalizing announced, and which revealed pairing permits it?
clauses.result: After cards are selected but before reveal, Calculator may declare equalize; it applies if both revealed cards are attacks.

clauses.clause: What changes and what stays fixed?
clauses.result: Reduce the higher attack’s value by the lower attack’s value; the lower attack retains its value.

clauses.clause: What values result from attacks 15 and 8?
clauses.result: The 15 becomes 7 (15 − 8); the 8 stays 8.

clauses.clause: What is the eligible role, optionality and phase for Chosen?
clauses.result: Main player only; optional; Reveal.

clauses.clause: How often and when may Divine Intervention be used, and how many cards are drawn?
clauses.result: Once per encounter, after revealing encounter cards, Chosen may use the power to draw three cards from the deck.

clauses.clause: What happens if there are no encounters among the drawn cards?
clauses.result: Discard all three; there is no further effect.

clauses.clause: What replacement or addition is allowed?
clauses.result: If any drawn card is an encounter card, Chosen may choose one to replace its own revealed encounter card, discarding the replaced card. If both its revealed card and the chosen replacement are attacks, Chosen may instead add the chosen card’s value to its revealed attack value.

clauses.clause: Where do replaced/unused cards go?
clauses.result: Discard the replaced card and all other drawn cards not used as the replacement/addition. Resolve with the new card or value.

clauses.clause: What is the eligible role, optionality and phase for Citadel?
clauses.result: As any player; optional; Planning.

clauses.clause: When, where and from what may citadels be placed?
clauses.result: During each player’s turn after destiny is drawn, Citadel may play an attack card from hand faceup next to any planet in any system as a citadel.

clauses.clause: Which portion requires power use?
clauses.result: Placing citadels does not require a power use; activating them does.

clauses.clause: When and how many citadels activate?
clauses.result: If a planet with at least one citadel is attacked, after encounter cards are selected but before reveal, Citadel may use its power to activate all citadels on that planet.

clauses.clause: What bonus applies?
clauses.result: Add the combined value of all activated citadels to the defense total.

clauses.clause: What happens to activated/unactivated citadels after defense wins or loses?
clauses.result: If activated and defense loses, discard the citadels. If defense wins, they stay; citadels not activated also stay.

clauses.clause: What is the eligible role, optionality and phase for Clone?
clauses.result: Main player only; optional; Resolution.

clauses.clause: When relative to outcome, compensation and discard may Replicate act?
clauses.result: After the encounter is resolved and any compensation has been claimed, Clone may use Replicate before its encounter card is discarded.

clauses.clause: Which card does it return to where?
clauses.result: Clone returns its own encounter card to its hand instead of discarding it.

clauses.clause: What is the eligible role, optionality and phase for Cudgel?
clauses.result: Main player only; mandatory; Resolution.

clauses.clause: What result and revealed card trigger Smash?
clauses.result: Cudgel must win an encounter in which it revealed an attack card.

clauses.clause: How many extra ships must which player lose, and who chooses them?
clauses.result: The opponent must lose extra ships of their own choice equal to the number of Cudgel’s ships in the encounter. These losses are in addition to normal losses.

clauses.clause: Does successfully making a deal count as a successful encounter, as a win for Cudgel or Barbarian, or both?
clauses.result: A deal is a successful encounter but not a win for either win-only power, so it triggers neither Cudgel nor Barbarian.

clauses.clause: Does changing Cudgel’s initially revealed negotiate into attack 42 with Human Wild satisfy the revealed-attack requirement?
clauses.result: No. Converting a revealed negotiate into an attack later does not count as having revealed an attack.

clauses.clause: What is the eligible role, optionality and phase for Dictator?
clauses.result: Not offense; mandatory; Destiny.

clauses.clause: On whose turns and when is Command used, and what selection information/choice does it give?
clauses.result: When not offense, before destiny is chosen, Dictator takes the destiny deck, looks through it and chooses any card to be played as if offense had drawn it.

clauses.clause: How is destiny handled on Dictator’s turn or when zapped?
clauses.result: On Dictator’s own turn, or any time the power is zapped, shuffle the remaining destiny cards and deal one randomly.

clauses.clause: What is the eligible role, optionality and phase for Fido?
clauses.result: As any player; optional; Resolution.

clauses.clause: When may Fetch act, and which card is offered to whom?
clauses.result: After encounter cards are discarded at the end of the encounter, Fido may retrieve one of the encounter cards actually played as such and offer it to another player.

clauses.clause: What happens on refusal versus acceptance?
clauses.result: If refused, Fido may keep the card. If accepted, the other player keeps it.

clauses.clause: What benefit may Fido receive?
clauses.result: After acceptance, Fido may either retrieve one ship from the warp or draw one card from the deck.

clauses.clause: What is the eligible role, optionality and phase for Filch?
clauses.result: Main player only; optional; Resolution.

clauses.clause: When may Theft act, whose encounter card is taken from where and added to whose hand?
clauses.result: After encounter cards are discarded at the end of the encounter, Filch may retrieve the opponent’s discarded encounter card from the discard pile and add it to Filch’s own hand.

clauses.clause: What is the eligible role, optionality and phase for Fodder?
clauses.result: Main player only; optional; Reveal.

clauses.clause: What pairing and timing permit Overwhelm?
clauses.result: After both main players reveal attack cards.

clauses.clause: Which hand attack values qualify relative to both revealed attacks?
clauses.result: Discarded attacks must each be higher than Fodder’s own played attack and lower than the opponent’s played attack.

clauses.clause: How many can be discarded, and how do they affect the total?
clauses.result: Fodder may discard any or all qualifying attack cards from hand; add their values to Fodder’s total.

clauses.clause: What is the eligible role, optionality and phase for Gambler?
clauses.result: Main player only; optional; Reveal.

clauses.clause: When does Bluff act relative to the opponent’s reveal, and what is announced?
clauses.result: After the opponent reveals their encounter card, Gambler may keep its own card facedown and state what the card is; Gambler may lie.

clauses.clause: What happens if the bluff is unchallenged?
clauses.result: Resolve as if Gambler’s statement were true, and place Gambler’s facedown card on the bottom of the deck instead of discarding it.

clauses.clause: On challenge, who loses how many ships from which locations, and how is the encounter then resolved?
clauses.result: Reveal Gambler’s card. If Gambler lied, Gambler loses to the warp as many ships as Gambler had in the encounter; if the statement was true, the opponent loses as many as the opponent had in the encounter. The penalty ships cannot be encounter ships; they are chosen outside the encounter from the losing player’s ships under their control. Then resolve the encounter normally using the revealed cards.

clauses.clause: What is the printed incompatible alien?
clauses.result: Sorcerer. The Gambler sheet says not to use Gambler with Sorcerer.

clauses.clause: What is the eligible role, optionality and phase for Grudge?
clauses.result: Main player only; mandatory; Alliance.

clauses.clause: When are tokens assigned, and to whom?
clauses.result: After alliances form, Grudge gives a token to each player invited by Grudge who did not ally with it. A player who initially committed at least one ship to Grudge counts as having allied even if those ships later leave.

clauses.clause: What happens for each win/deal branch?
clauses.result: If Grudge wins or makes a deal, each token holder discards the token and loses one ship of their choice to the warp.

clauses.clause: What happens for each loss/failed-deal branch?
clauses.result: If Grudge loses or the deal fails, each token holder discards the token and loses four ships of their choice to the warp.

clauses.clause: Who chooses penalty ships, and which ships are ineligible?
clauses.result: Each penalized token holder chooses their own penalty ships; ships used to ally with the other side cannot be lost for the penalty. If a required outside-encounter loss has no eligible ships, lose none.

clauses.clause: What is the eligible role, optionality and phase for Hacker?
clauses.result: Main player only; optional; Resolution.

clauses.clause: When collecting compensation, from whose hand may Hack take cards and who looks/chooses them?
clauses.result: When Hacker collects compensation, it may choose a player to collect from, whether or not that player is the opponent; Hacker looks through that player’s hand and chooses the compensation cards.

clauses.clause: When Hacker owes compensation, who selects what the opponent receives?
clauses.result: When an opponent collects compensation from Hacker, Hacker may select the cards the opponent gets.

clauses.clause: What is the eligible role, optionality and phase for Hate?
clauses.result: Offense only; mandatory; Start Turn.

clauses.clause: When does Rage act, and what must Hate discard?
clauses.result: At the start of its own turn, Hate uses the power and first chooses and discards a card from its hand.

clauses.clause: What alternatives does each other player have?
clauses.result: Each other player must either discard a card of the same type or lose three ships to the warp chosen by Hate. If the chosen card is an attack, they must discard an attack meeting the printed threshold; a player without a qualifying card loses ships instead.

clauses.clause: What attack threshold does the original sheet print, and who selects lost ships?
clauses.result: The sheet permits an attack of equal or higher value than Hate’s discarded attack; Hate chooses the ships lost.

clauses.clause: What happens if Hate then lacks encounter cards?
clauses.result: If Hate has no encounter cards after using its power, it draws a new hand.

clauses.clause: What is the eligible role, optionality and phase for Healer?
clauses.result: As any player; optional; Start Turn, Regroup, Destiny, Launch, Alliance, Planning, Reveal and Resolution.

clauses.clause: What event and whose losses permit Heal?
clauses.result: When another player loses ships to the warp or has ships removed from the game. Healer cannot heal itself.

clauses.clause: How many of that event’s ships return and where?
clauses.result: Return all ships just lost to that player; the healed player places them on any of their colonies.

clauses.clause: What card benefit is earned, and can several players be healed?
clauses.result: Healer earns one card from the deck for each player healed and may heal several players during an encounter.

clauses.clause: Does healing remove compensation?
clauses.result: No. Ships reach the warp before healing, so healing does not prevent compensation.

clauses.clause: What is the eligible role, optionality and phase for Human?
clauses.result: Main player or ally only; mandatory; Reveal.

clauses.clause: When does Humanity act, and what bonus does it add to which side?
clauses.result: After encounter cards are revealed, Human adds 4 to its own side’s total.

clauses.clause: What happens if this use is zapped?
clauses.result: Human’s own side automatically wins the encounter.

clauses.clause: What is the eligible role, optionality and phase for Kamikaze?
clauses.result: Main player only; optional; Planning.

clauses.clause: When may Sacrifice act, and how many ships from where may be sacrificed?
clauses.result: Before encounter cards are selected, Kamikaze may send up to four of its ships from any of its colonies to the warp.

clauses.clause: What cards result?
clauses.result: Draw two cards from the deck for every ship sent.

clauses.clause: What happens to those ships if the use is zapped?
clauses.result: The sacrificed ships are not lost to the warp.

clauses.clause: What is the eligible role, optionality and phase for Loser?
clauses.result: Main player only; optional; Planning.

clauses.clause: When is Upset declared, and what card-selection restriction follows?
clauses.result: Before encounter cards are selected, Loser may declare an upset. Both main players must then play attack cards if able.

clauses.clause: How does Upset change the outcome?
clauses.result: After resolution, the previously winning side loses and the previously losing side wins.

clauses.clause: When does the reversal happen relative to other effects, including zapped Human?
clauses.result: The reversal occurs after all other game effects have resolved, including Human’s power being zapped.

clauses.clause: What is the eligible role, optionality and phase for Machine?
clauses.result: Offense only; optional; Resolution.

clauses.clause: After what outcomes may Continuity grant another encounter?
clauses.result: After completing an encounter, whether successful or not, Machine may take another encounter.

clauses.clause: How many encounters may its turn contain and what hand requirement remains?
clauses.result: The turn is not limited to two encounters; Machine may continue as long as at least one encounter card remains in its hand.

clauses.clause: What is the eligible role, optionality and phase for Macron under the retained erratum?
clauses.result: Main player or ally; mandatory; Launch, Alliance and Reveal.

clauses.clause: When are Mass’s launch/ally limitation and ship-strength uses made?
clauses.result: As offense, use before launching; as an ally, after allies are invited; as a main player or ally, use after encounter cards are revealed for the ship-strength effect.

clauses.clause: What ship limit applies to offense/allies?
clauses.result: Macron as offense or ally may send only one of its ships into the encounter.

clauses.clause: How much is each ship worth for total versus compensation/rewards, and does defense itself have a one-ship launch limit?
clauses.result: Each Macron ship adds 4 to its side’s total and counts as two ships for compensation or defender rewards. The one-ship limit applies when Macron is offense or ally; it imposes no launch limit on a defending Macron.

clauses.clause: When a Virus Wild or Super effect specifies a number of ships, does each Macron ship count as one or four?
clauses.result: One: count each physical Macron ship as one ship for an effect asking for a number of ships; the four is its combat strength.

clauses.clause: What is the eligible role, optionality and phase for Masochist?
clauses.result: As any player; mandatory; Regroup.

clauses.clause: When exactly is Hurt Yourself checked, and what lost-ship locations count?
clauses.result: At the start of any player’s Regroup phase, before offense retrieves a warp ship; Masochist uses the power to win if all its ships are lost, including ships in the warp, removed from the game, or captured by other players.

clauses.clause: What is the alternate win condition, is it lost for too few home colonies, and can Masochist still win normally?
clauses.result: Its alternate win requires all its ships to have been lost. Masochist does not lose its power for having fewer than three home colonies and may also win normally.

clauses.clause: If an in-scope alien effect explicitly causes an immediate game win, must play continue until the end of Resolution?
clauses.result: No. An expressly immediate win ends the game when that effect resolves; it need not wait for the end-of-Resolution ordinary victory check.

clauses.clause: What can interrupt that winning effect before it resolves?
clauses.result: A Cosmic Zap or a specific interrupt can stop it before it resolves.

clauses.clause: What is the eligible role, optionality and phase for Mind?
clauses.result: As any player; optional; Alliance.

clauses.clause: When and whose hand may Knowledge inspect?
clauses.result: Before allies are invited, Mind may inspect the entire hand of one main player.

clauses.clause: How does being a main player restrict that target?
clauses.result: If Mind is a main player, it may inspect the opponent’s hand.

clauses.clause: What may Mind reveal to other players?
clauses.result: Mind may not tell other players what cards it saw in a player’s hand through its power.

clauses.clause: What is the eligible role, optionality and phase for Mirror?
clauses.result: Main player only; optional; Planning.

clauses.clause: When is Reversal declared, and which revealed cards are changed?
clauses.result: After encounter cards are selected but before reveal, Mirror may call reversal; reverse the digits of any attack cards revealed in that encounter.

clauses.clause: How are digits treated, and what values result from 15, 20 and 08?
clauses.result: Reverse the digits: 15 becomes 51, 20 becomes 02, and 08 becomes 80.

clauses.clause: What is the eligible role, optionality and phase for Miser?
clauses.result: As any player; optional; Start Turn, Regroup, Destiny, Launch, Alliance, Planning, Reveal and Resolution.

clauses.clause: What extra hands and choice are given at setup?
clauses.result: Deal two separate eight-card hands; Miser looks at them and chooses one to set aside facedown on its sheet as the hoard.

clauses.clause: How may Hoard substitute for the ordinary hand?
clauses.result: Whenever Miser wishes to play a card, it may use its power to play it from the hoard instead of its ordinary hand.

clauses.clause: Can gains be put there, or can opponents inspect/draw from it?
clauses.result: No. Gained cards cannot be added to the hoard, and other players may not look at or draw cards from it.

clauses.clause: When and how can the hoard be replaced?
clauses.result: If the hoard has no encounter cards, Miser may reveal and discard it, then receive a new eight-card hoard.

clauses.clause: What is the eligible role, optionality and phase for Mite?
clauses.result: Offense only; mandatory; Launch.

clauses.clause: When and at what defense hand-size threshold does Bluster act?
clauses.result: Before allies are invited, if defense has more than three cards.

clauses.clause: What two alternatives does defense have, and how are cards discarded?
clauses.result: Defense either discards down to three cards at random or lets Mite establish a colony on the targeted world.

clauses.clause: What are ship destinations and encounter status under each choice?
clauses.result: If defense discards, the encounter continues normally. If it grants the colony, Mite lands any of its ships in the gate on the target; they coexist with the defense’s ships, which do not go to the warp, and the encounter immediately ends successfully.

clauses.clause: What is the eligible role, optionality and phase for Mutant?
clauses.result: Main player only; optional; Alliance.

clauses.clause: When and at what hand size may Regenerate act?
clauses.result: Before allies are invited, Mutant may use it if it has fewer than eight cards.

clauses.clause: From which sources and in what sequence/randomness are cards taken, and when does drawing stop?
clauses.result: Draw cards one at a time, at random, from any player or players or from the deck, until Mutant’s hand has eight cards.

clauses.clause: What is the eligible role, optionality and phase for Observer?
clauses.result: Main player or ally; mandatory; Resolution.

clauses.clause: In each role, whose ships are protected?
clauses.result: As an ally, Observer protects all of its own ships, including ships outside the encounter. As a main player, it protects all of its allies’ ships, including remote losses.

clauses.clause: During what phase and from which loss destination are they returned to where?
clauses.result: Protection applies during Resolution when ships would be lost to the warp: an ally returns its ships to any of its own colonies; a main player lets each affected ally return those ships to colonies of that ally’s choice.

clauses.clause: What is the eligible role, optionality and phase for Oracle?
clauses.result: Main player only; mandatory; Planning.

clauses.clause: When does Foresee act, and whose card is played in what manner first?
clauses.result: Before encounter cards are selected, Oracle forces the opponent to play an encounter card faceup.

clauses.clause: When does Oracle then select and play its own?
clauses.result: After seeing the opponent’s card, Oracle selects and plays its own encounter card.

clauses.clause: What is the eligible role, optionality and phase for Pacifist?
clauses.result: Main player only; mandatory; Reveal.

clauses.clause: Which revealed pairing triggers Peace and who wins?
clauses.result: If Pacifist reveals negotiate and the opponent reveals attack, Pacifist uses the power to win the encounter.

clauses.clause: What happens when both reveal negotiate?
clauses.result: Attempt a deal as usual.

clauses.clause: What is the eligible role, optionality and phase for Parasite?
clauses.result: Not a main player; optional; Alliance.

clauses.clause: When may Infest act, and what invitation and side choices does it change?
clauses.result: When it is Parasite’s turn to ally, it may join either side as if invited even if it was not invited.

clauses.clause: How many ships are sent?
clauses.result: One to four ships as usual.

clauses.clause: Can it override an effect that specifically prevents alliance?
clauses.result: No. Parasite cannot bypass an effect that specifically prevents alliance, such as Force Field.

clauses.clause: What is the eligible role, optionality and phase for Philanthropist?
clauses.result: Main player or ally; optional; Alliance.

clauses.clause: When may Giving act, how many cards from where go to which eligible recipient?
clauses.result: After alliances are formed, Philanthropist may give one card from its hand to either main player; if Philanthropist is a main player, it must give the card to the opponent.

clauses.clause: When can that card be used?
clauses.result: The recipient immediately adds the card to its hand and may play it normally.

clauses.clause: Under what own-hand/role condition is a new hand drawn?
clauses.result: If afterward Philanthropist has no encounter cards in its hand and is a main player, it draws a new hand.

clauses.clause: What is the eligible role, optionality and phase for Reincarnator?
clauses.result: Main player or ally; mandatory; Resolution.

clauses.clause: What results trigger Reincarnation, and where is the replacement drawn from?
clauses.result: Losing an encounter or failing a deal triggers a random draw of a replacement alien power from the unused pile.

clauses.clause: Which replacement candidates are rejected?
clauses.result: Redraw any alien with Game Setup text or one not allowed in the current game.

clauses.clause: What happens on later losses, and what old power remains?
clauses.result: If Reincarnator loses a later encounter, discard the current alien and draw a new one; Reincarnator retains its own power while using the other alien’s power.

clauses.clause: Under the original printed copying conditional, which powers may another alien copy, and what happens when that copier loses?
clauses.result: An alien able to copy a power may copy both Reincarnator and the currently reincarnated power. If it loses an encounter while copying, it must reincarnate and loses its original power.

clauses.clause: What is the eligible role, optionality and phase for Remora?
clauses.result: As any player; optional; Start Turn, Regroup, Destiny, Launch, Alliance, Planning, Reveal and Resolution.

clauses.clause: What warp retrieval event permits Cling, and how much is obtained?
clauses.result: Whenever another player retrieves one or more ships from the warp, Remora may retrieve one of its own warp ships.

clauses.clause: What deck draw event permits Cling, how much is obtained and where does it come from?
clauses.result: Whenever another player draws one or more cards from the cosmic deck, Remora may draw one card from that deck.

clauses.clause: What same-encounter retrieval restriction applies?
clauses.result: Remora may not retrieve a ship in the same encounter in which it went to the warp.

clauses.clause: What is the eligible role, optionality and phase for Reserve?
clauses.result: Main player or ally; optional; Reveal.

clauses.clause: When may Reinforce turn which attack cards into what value, and how many may it use?
clauses.result: After encounter cards are revealed, Reserve may play one or more attack cards of 06 or less from hand as reinforcement cards with their listed values.

clauses.clause: What cost cancels another player’s reinforcement, and where does that canceled card go?
clauses.result: When another player plays a reinforcement, Reserve may use its power and discard a negotiate card to cancel it; discard the canceled reinforcement.

clauses.clause: What is the eligible role, optionality and phase for Shadow?
clauses.result: As any player; mandatory; Destiny.

clauses.clause: Which destiny draws trigger Execute?
clauses.result: Any other player’s color destiny, or a special destiny targeting another player, triggers it whenever drawn.

clauses.clause: Who chooses whose ship from which location?
clauses.result: Shadow chooses one ship belonging to the player indicated by the qualifying destiny, selects it from any colony of Shadow’s choice, and sends it to the warp.

clauses.clause: How is wild handled, and must its target match offense’s chosen defense?
clauses.result: On a wild destiny Shadow may execute one ship of any other player, regardless of whom offense chooses to attack; the target need not match the chosen defense.

clauses.clause: What is the eligible role, optionality and phase for Sorcerer?
clauses.result: Main player only; optional; Planning.

clauses.clause: When relative to selection/reveal does Magic act, and what is switched?
clauses.result: After both encounter cards are selected but before reveal, Sorcerer may switch its card with the opponent’s.

clauses.clause: Which card does each player reveal afterward?
clauses.result: The opponent reveals the card Sorcerer originally selected, and Sorcerer reveals the opponent’s originally selected card.

clauses.clause: What is the eligible role, optionality and phase for Spiff?
clauses.result: Offense only; optional; Resolution.

clauses.clause: What card pairing and losing margin permit Crash Land?
clauses.result: When Spiff is offense and loses an encounter in which both main players revealed attacks, it may use the power if it lost by 10 or more.

clauses.clause: How many ships escape what loss and land where?
clauses.result: Spiff may land one of its own ships that would otherwise be lost to the warp on the winning defensive planet.

clauses.clause: Which coexistence restrictions remain?
clauses.result: The ship coexists with ships there, but Crash Land does not allow coexistence where a place or alien says otherwise.

clauses.clause: Does the margin condition include a low-total-wins encounter?
clauses.result: Yes. The 10-or-more margin condition includes low-total-wins encounters.

clauses.clause: What is the eligible role, optionality and phase for Tick-Tock?
clauses.result: As any player; mandatory; Resolution.

clauses.clause: How many tokens are set up in the standard five-planet game?
clauses.result: Ten tokens.

clauses.clause: Which two types of events remove tokens?
clauses.result: A win as defense, or a successful deal between any two players, removes one token.

clauses.clause: What happens at the final token, and can Tick-Tock still win normally?
clauses.result: When no tokens remain, Tick-Tock immediately wins; it may also win normally.

clauses.clause: What is the eligible role, optionality and phase for Trader?
clauses.result: Main player only; optional; Planning.

clauses.clause: When may Transference act, which hands are exchanged and who keeps which hand afterward?
clauses.result: Before encounter cards are selected, Trader may trade hands with the opponent; afterward each keeps the new hand received.

clauses.clause: What is the eligible role, optionality and phase for Tripler?
clauses.result: Main player only; mandatory; Reveal.

clauses.clause: When does Thrice act, and what card type is required?
clauses.result: After revealing an attack card.

clauses.clause: What happens at values 10-or-less versus above 10, and what rounding applies?
clauses.result: An attack value of 10 or less is tripled; a value above 10 is divided by three and rounded up.

clauses.clause: Calculate attacks 10 and 11.
clauses.result: 10 becomes 30. 11 becomes 4 (11 ÷ 3 rounded up).

clauses.clause: What is the eligible role, optionality and phase for Vacuum?
clauses.result: As any player; mandatory; Start Turn, Regroup, Destiny, Launch, Alliance, Planning, Reveal and Resolution.

clauses.clause: What event triggers Catharsis, and how many additional ships may be lost?
clauses.result: Whenever Vacuum’s own ships are lost to the warp, it may take along up to an equal number of other ships. These losses are additional to the ordinary losses.

clauses.clause: Who chooses targets/quantities versus exact colony sources?
clauses.result: Vacuum specifies the affected players and how many ships each loses; each targeted player chooses the colony or colonies from which their ships come.

clauses.clause: Can Vacuum target itself?
clauses.result: No; it cannot target itself.

clauses.clause: Are these losses additional to ordinary losses?
clauses.result: Yes, they are in addition to the normal encounter losses.

clauses.clause: What is the eligible role, optionality and phase for Virus?
clauses.result: Main player only; mandatory; Reveal.

clauses.clause: When does Multiply act, and how are its own ships and attack card combined?
clauses.result: After revealing an attack, Virus multiplies its own attack-card value by the number of its own ships in the encounter, instead of adding those ships.

clauses.clause: How are allied ships counted?
clauses.result: Allied ships are added to the total normally.

clauses.clause: What total results from attack 8, three own ships and two allied ships?
clauses.result: Three own ships × attack 8 = 24; add two allied ships for a total of 26.

clauses.clause: What is the eligible role, optionality and phase for Void?
clauses.result: Main player only; mandatory; Resolution.

clauses.clause: What result triggers Eradicate, and whose ships go to which destination?
clauses.result: When Void wins an encounter, it removes the losing side’s ships from the game instead of sending them to the warp.

clauses.clause: What minimum number of surviving ships is protected in this standard game?
clauses.result: A player may not be reduced below the number of ships needed for five foreign colonies: five surviving ships.

clauses.clause: Where do excess losses go, and in the six-ship/three-loss example how many are eradicated versus sent to warp?
clauses.result: Ships beyond the protected minimum are eradicated; ships that cannot be eradicated because of the five-ship limit go to the warp. With six ships and three due to be lost, one is eradicated and two go to the warp.

clauses.clause: What is the eligible role, optionality and phase for Vulch?
clauses.result: As any player; mandatory; Start Turn, Regroup, Destiny, Launch, Alliance, Planning, Reveal and Resolution.

clauses.clause: Whose discarded artifacts trigger Salvage, and does played versus unplayed matter?
clauses.result: Any other player’s discarded artifact triggers it, whether or not the artifact was played.

clauses.clause: Can Vulch salvage its own played artifacts?
clauses.result: No. Its own played artifacts are discarded normally and cannot be salvaged.

clauses.clause: What special reveal/retention/new-draw procedure applies when refreshing a hand?
clauses.result: When drawing a new hand, Vulch retains old artifacts after revealing them, then draws eight new cards in addition to those retained artifacts.

clauses.clause: What is the eligible role, optionality and phase for Warpish?
clauses.result: Main player only; mandatory; Reveal.

clauses.clause: When and with which revealed card may Necromancy act?
clauses.result: After revealing an attack card.

clauses.clause: Whose warp ships count, and how much do they add?
clauses.result: Every ship in the warp counts, whether it belongs to Warpish or anyone else; add 1 to Warpish’s total per ship.

clauses.clause: What is the eligible role, optionality and phase for Warrior?
clauses.result: Main player only; mandatory; Reveal.

clauses.clause: Under the erratum, in which role/results are tokens gained and in what quantities?
clauses.result: After an encounter where Warrior was a main player, gain one token for a win or deal and two tokens for a loss or failed deal.

clauses.clause: When/how is the combat bonus used, what card type is required and are tokens spent?
clauses.result: As a main player after revealing an attack, Warrior adds 1 to its total per sheet token; tokens are not discarded.

clauses.clause: If Warrior’s power is Cosmic Zapped, does it still gain experience from a qualifying result?
clauses.result: Yes. Gaining experience does not require a power use and continues even if the combat bonus is zapped.

clauses.clause: What is the eligible role, optionality and phase for Will?
clauses.result: Offense only; mandatory; Destiny.

clauses.clause: Under the timing correction, when does Choice act and how may it change opponent/location?
clauses.result: After drawing destiny, Will may choose to encounter any alien on any planet of its choice instead of the alien indicated by destiny.

clauses.clause: What third-player-system colony requirement remains?
clauses.result: Will may choose another player’s colony in a third player’s system only if that colony actually exists; it may still encounter a home-system owner on that owner’s empty home planet.

clauses.clause: Do other effects of the drawn destiny card still occur?
clauses.result: Yes. Other effects caused by the drawn destiny card, including Shadow, still occur.

clauses.clause: What is the eligible role, optionality and phase for Zombie?
clauses.result: As any player; mandatory; Start Turn, Regroup, Destiny, Launch, Alliance, Planning, Reveal and Resolution.

clauses.clause: When does Immortality prevent a warp loss, and where are ships sent instead?
clauses.result: Whenever Zombie’s ships would be lost to the warp, they instead return to any existing colonies Zombie has.

clauses.clause: Which additional deal clause does not require power use?
clauses.result: As part of a deal, Zombie may free the negotiating opponent’s ships from the warp; this liberation is not a power use.

clauses.clause: Who may be liberated and where do freed ships go?
clauses.result: Only the negotiating opponent’s ships may be liberated, returning them to that opponent’s existing colonies; Zombie may not free a third player’s ships.

clauses.clause: Is there a numerical limit on the number Zombie may liberate?
clauses.result: No numerical cap applies.

## Overview

This summary covers the original **Fantasy Flight English 2008 CE01** game for 3–5 players, including its fifty original aliens, normal flare system and applicable official FAQ rulings. Optional Technology, Four Planets, Hidden Powers, Rotating Powers and Freewheeling Flares are excluded, as are Anniversary bonus content and all expansions. Read an individual card's printed effect and timing when playing it; the flare rules below explain the shared system rather than reproduce every flare card.

Each player leads an alien trying to establish five **foreign colonies**. A colony is one or more ships of one color on one planet; extra ships on that planet do not make extra colonies. Several colors can coexist there, each with its own colony. Home colonies are in your own system; foreign colonies are outside it. Five foreign planets can all be in one other system. Alien powers override conflicting general rules.

U1.text:
## Setup

1. Put the warp in the center. Each player takes five planets of one color, places four of their twenty ships on each, and places their colony marker beside the warp's 0 space.
2. Remove destiny cards naming unused player colors; shuffle the rest, including wilds and specials.
3. Shuffle the flares, deal two to each player, and give them the matching alien sheets. Each secretly chooses one alien, initially placing it facedown, and returns the other sheet to the box. This is the standard selection procedure; Hidden Powers is a separate excluded variant. The original text does not specify when standard-game sheets are turned faceup; unlike the optional Hidden Powers rule, it gives no explicit reveal window. This source gap is recorded rather than supplying a new setup rule. Green/yellow/red indicate recommended experience, not strength. Beginners may start with green aliens without flares.
4. Add **both flares dealt to every player**, including rejected aliens' flares, to the cosmic deck. Add random extras if needed to reach ten flares total; shuffle. Deal eight-card hands. Keep card faces private unless an effect allows showing them.
5. Draw destiny until a player color appears; that player starts. Shuffle the drawn card back into the destiny deck. Play passes left thereafter.

Apply printed alien Game Setup instructions as well. If chosen aliens have a printed incompatibility, remove the alien bearing the restriction, keeping the unrestricted alien. Its player may use their originally rejected alien or draw a replacement unused flare and take that alien, redrawing conflicts. Gambler's printed restriction is **Do not use with Sorcerer**; using them together is an optional FAQ-permitted relaxation, outside this standard setup.

### 1. Regroup

Offense must retrieve one of its ships from the warp if available, placing it on any existing home or foreign colony. The original rulebook puts this retrieved ship directly in the gate if offense has no colonies. The FAQ adds that a player who has no colonies or ships on their turn may instead place the Regroup ship on any home planet. Ordinary relocation with no colony to receive ships sends them to the warp; the stated Regroup exceptions take precedence.

U3.text:
### 2. Destiny

Draw destiny to determine the defense and target system. **When only one card remains, do not draw it**: shuffle it with the destiny discards, then draw from the new deck.

- Another player's color: encounter that player in their home system.
- Your own color: redraw, or target one chosen foreign colony in your home system, making its owner the defense. Other colonies there are bystanders. You can instead aim at a home planet with **no ships of any color**, moving up to four of your ships from any of your other existing home or foreign colonies onto that empty home planet to reclaim it automatically. This counts as a win and successful encounter, proceeds only through Launch, and can qualify you for a second encounter.
- Wild: choose another player and encounter them in their home system.
- Special: follow its conditions, defense and location. The original rulebook's illustrated special card chooses the other player with the most current foreign colonies, excluding offense. Break a tie toward offense's left, choosing the first tied eligible player there; encounter that player in their home system (rulebook p7). For color-dependent effects such as Shadow, treat it as the designated defense's color. If a special card designates you as the defense, the original rulebook also permits trying to drive out a foreign colony in your home system: choose one other player's colony as the defense; all other colonies are unaffected bystanders.

Destiny hazard symbols have no effect in this base game. Ordinarily you cannot attack a player's foreign colony in a third player's system: a color/wild/special targets its defense in that player's home system, while your own color permits driving out a foreign colony in your own system. If you already have colonies on **all planets in the defensive system**, draw destiny again.

U4.text:
### 3. Launch

The offense chooses one planet in the destiny-indicated system and aims the gate at it. Place one to four offense ships on the **wide end of the hyperspace gate**, drawn from any combination of the offense's existing home and foreign colonies. You may strip a colony, but removing its last ship immediately eliminates it. Ships returning from an encounter or warp cannot return to that now-empty location as though it remained your colony.

Defense cannot add or subtract ships on the target. The owner of a home system defends their planet even with zero ships there. Other colors' colonies are **bystanders**: they add nothing to the defense and the encounter result does not harm them. When driving out a foreign colony, target only that one color's colony; all other colors are bystanders.

If you cannot put any ship in the gate or the last offensive ship is removed, continue the encounter. Winning alone does not give offense a colony without a ship to land, unless a specific effect allows it.

### 4. Alliance

Offense names invited allies first; they wait to answer. Defense then invites allies, possibly including the same players. Neither main player may invite the other. Starting with the player left of offense and proceeding clockwise, each other player accepts one invitation or declines all, then commits ships before the next player decides. You may join only one side or neither; normally an invitation is required.

Each ally contributes one to four ships from any of their colonies. Offensive allies place them on the gate; defensive allies place them beside the target planet, **not on it**. The FAQ nevertheless considers defensive allies in the gate for effects referring to that location. Parasite changes invitation eligibility.

U6.text:
### Attack against attack

Each side's total is its main player's attack value plus all ships on its side: offense and offensive allies in the gate; defense on the target plus defensive allies beside it. Higher total wins; **defense wins ties**. Powers and played cards may change this calculation or the winner.

- **Offense wins:** all offense and offensive ally ships land on the target, establishing or reinforcing each color's colony. Defense and defensive ally ships go to warp. Bystanders survive. Advance a colony marker only for a newly established foreign colony, not reinforcement of an existing colony.
- **Defense wins:** defending and bystander colonies stay. Offense and offensive allies go to warp. Defensive allies return their committed ships to any existing own colonies, even different origins; helping defend does not grant a colony on the defended planet. Each defensive ally must collect **one defender reward per ship contributed**. For each contributed ship, draw one cosmic-deck card or retrieve one own warp ship to any own colony; combine these choices freely. The ordinary rule does not permit declining these rewards. Declare the full mix of card draws and warp-ship retrievals **before taking any rewards**; do not inspect an initial draw before deciding the remaining sources (official FAQ p8's base-relevant reward-source rule).

### Attack against negotiate: compensation

The negotiate player automatically loses; resolve the winner's ship destinations normally. The losing main player randomly takes one card from the opponent's hand for each of **their own ships actually lost to the warp**. Exclude allied losses: allies receive no compensation. If the opponent lacks sufficient cards, take the entire hand. Cards are taken without seeing their faces. For random hand-card selection, including compensation, you may see which card backs you select; “at random” means without seeing card faces (FAQ p5). Compensation is stolen hand cards; defender rewards are deck draws and/or warp retrieval.

No compensation for ships prevented from reaching the warp (Zombie/Observer) or removed by Void. Healer returning ships **after** they enter the warp does not remove compensation eligibility. Special winners such as Human/Pacifist can change who wins; compensation still requires the relevant attack-versus-negotiate condition.

### Negotiate against negotiate: making a deal

Both sides' allies return ships to their own colonies, gain nothing and cannot participate in the deal. The main players have **one minute**. They may transfer cards from their hands and/or each grant the other **one colony on a planet where the giver already has a colony**, including a foreign colony. The recipient can use any own ships not in the warp. Existing ships coexist; the giver need not vacate, and vacating would eliminate the colony being offered. Return any remaining gate ships to offense's colonies.

A successful deal must actually transfer at least one card or colony; it may be one-sided. You cannot agree to do nothing. Tangible terms are restricted to permitted cards/colonies and specific power/card exceptions such as Zombie's liberation; future promises are unenforceable. Card terms may be explicit or vague but must be truthful and honored (if you promise your highest attack, give it). If time expires without agreement, **each main player loses three ships of their choice to the warp**, and offense cannot take an ordinary second encounter. Successful deals qualify for an ordinary second encounter but do not trigger win-only powers.

### Morph

The single base Morph becomes an exact copy of the opponent's initially revealed encounter card: attack copies its initial value, negotiate becomes negotiate. Resolve that pairing normally. Subsequent modifications of the opponent's card do not automatically carry over to Morph; Morph can be modified separately. For example, Tripler revealing Morph against attack12 copies12 and divides its own copy to4; Tripler revealing12 against Morph changes its own12 to4, while opponent's Morph remains12. After resolution, Morph returns to its normal identity and is normally discarded with the other revealed encounter card, unless an effect changes its destination. If two Morphs could be played against each other, both sides would lose all involved ships to warp; there is only one in this base deck.

For encounter resolution (card types/values, totals, winner/loser, deals, compensation/rewards and involved ship disposition), use current modified card type/value. Other effects normally refer to original printed identity. Morph's printed identity remains Morph. A later card conversion does not change what card was originally revealed for a reveal-trigger condition.

### Artifacts and reinforcements

Artifacts are not encounter cards. Follow each artifact's printed effect, permitted role and timing; normally discard after play. **Any player, including an uninvolved bystander, may play Cosmic Zap** on an otherwise legal power use. It cancels that use, including your own, and prevents further uses for that encounter. Cards that cancel cards follow their own printed instructions.

Reinforcements are not encounter cards. During Reveal, after encounter cards are revealed, either main player and any ally may play them to add the card's **printed amount to either side's total**, including the opposing side. Players may respond with further reinforcements until all pass; then resolve using the new totals. Bystanders cannot play them merely because they are present on the planet.

**Official FAQ wording conflict:** FAQ p3 explicitly permits involved players to play reinforcements on either side regardless of the revealed card types; p4 also answers “Can you play a reinforcement card on a negotiate?” with “No.” The ordinary attack-total procedure above is unambiguous. The supplied FAQ does not explain whether its p4 answer means a reinforcement cannot change the negotiate card itself or contradicts its p3 permission. These statements should be checked against a publisher clarification before ruling on that disputed non-attack case.

### Flare system

Flares are not encounter cards. Each has printed Wild and Super effects, usage roles and timing. Normally use Wild; if it is your own alien's flare and your power is available, **you must use Super**, not choose Wild. If your power is lost or zapped, you can use only Wild until your power returns.

Return a flare to hand **immediately after its effect finishes**, rather than discard it, unless its effect states otherwise. A player may play **at most one flare per encounter**, and an individual flare can be used **only once per encounter even if it changes hands**. A Card Zap targeting the flare counts against the player's limit. Prevention of play differs from cancellation after play: see Anti-Matter's FAQ exception. If a Super enables a power use, that power can still be Cosmic Zapped even outside its usual role/phase. The flare remains in hand rather than being discarded or forced to Wild; Only Wild is available for an otherwise legal play while the power is zapped. Zapping the enabled power does not undo the already-played flare or permit a second play of it in the same encounter; the ordinary per-player and per-flare limits still apply. When your own Wild would otherwise be handed to your alien, keep it after resolution.

The FAQ quotes these Super effect timing clauses; they do not make a flare apply automatically in later encounters. Follow the full card for its other conditions and legal play.

|---|---|
